hook.line: What is something in SEO nobody knows to do?
hook.visual: Man in a puffer jacket at an outdoor cafe table, coffee cup in hand, looking at the lens; the question sits as large white sentence captions across his chest.

beats.what: The question is asked over a calm, still shot of him holding a coffee, like a street-interview prompt.
Answer in one line: add a preferred sources badge to your website (finger raised).
A Google 'Top stories' screenshot card pops above the captions as he lists AI Overviews, AI Mode, Discover.
Calls it a new Google feature everybody is sleeping on.
Google Search Central docs card with a blue arrow: paste the documentation into your favourite AI.
The blue 'make me a preferred source on Google' button appears as proof: done in five minutes.
A green version of the button shows it can be restyled.
A news headline card says it is a global SEO signal; closes on 'your site does better for everybody'.

why_it_works: Opens with a question that frames the tip as insider knowledge ('nobody knows'), then answers it within about 3 s, so there is no wait.
Each claim gets a small screenshot card above the captions (Top stories, Search Central docs, the button, a news headline), so proof arrives as the claim is spoken.
Short and single-idea (39 s, one tip), with a high loop score (0.796) that invites rewatching.
The relaxed cafe setting with a coffee feels like advice from a friend, not an ad.
weaknesses: No CTA at all; nothing asks to follow or comment.
Captions and cards sit across his chest in the middle band, with 95% of text outside the safe area.
Zero motion events and only 3 cuts; the cards just appear without animation.
for_robert: Answer the hook question in the first 3 s, then drop one small proof card (screenshot, docs, headline) above the caption for each claim; Fred could slide each card in and nudge it away.
